sentences.text: This ancient crocodile has been placed within both the families Crocodylidae and Gavialidae.
It is also assigned to the subfamily Tomistominae.
However, its exact classification remains uncertain because the position of Tomistominae within the order Crocodylia is controversial.
Fossils of this creature have been found in Colombia, Brazil, Jamaica, and possibly Florida and South Carolina.
A lower jaw dated to the Lutetian stage of the Eocene found in Jamaica was described as the species C. kugleri in 1969.
Isolated teeth attributed to Charactosuchus from Florida and South Carolina date to the early Pliocene.
This animal lived from the Lutetian to the Tortonian stages, spanning approximately 48.07 to 7.246 million years ago.
The type species, C. fieldsi, inhabited the Villavieja Formation at La Venta in Colombia during the Middle Miocene.
Remains have also been recovered from the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela and the Solimões Formation in Brazil.
It is debated whether C. kugleri is a valid species or a synonym of Dollosuchus.
The theory that Charactosuchus migrated from North America to South America is no longer accepted, while its presence in Jamaica suggests a possible European origin via land bridges.
